outcome: Help authorised student-success teams identify support needs earlier and coordinate humane interventions.
overview: Warning signs of disengagement sit fragmented across attendance, engagement, academic and service systems, so support often arrives after problems become severe. This solution combines those signals into explainable risk indicators and recommended support pathways for authorised student-success teams. It never labels, disciplines, excludes or automatically contacts a learner — every alert routes to a named human reviewer, with fairness monitoring and a full record of actions and overrides. A retrospective validation on one or two historical terms tests the indicators before any live pilot, targeting a 40% reduction in the median time from an agreed warning signal to a documented human review.

benefits.text: Reach struggling learners earlier — target 40% faster from warning signal to human review
benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue; to validate against a historical-term baseline
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on signal quality and counsellor capacity — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Protect tuition and funding by improving retention in a controlled pilot cohort
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Retention attribution has causality limits that are reported, not hidden

benefits.text: Give counsellors prioritised, explainable caseloads with every action and override logged
benefits.source: Reference design — explanation, logging and fairness reporting are structural
benefits.limits: Explanations cover the indicators used; they do not diagnose causes of disengagement

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (UAE, KSA); learner data never leaves the institution’s tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No defined support services or named case owners to act on alerts
notFor.why: An early-warning queue without intervention capacity creates risk without helping anyone

notFor.situation: The institution wants automated messaging or sanctions triggered by risk scores
notFor.why: The design prohibits automated contact and disciplinary use — indicators inform humans only

notFor.situation: No lawful basis for processing the attendance and engagement data involved
notFor.why: Student-data protection requires an approved privacy assessment before any modelling

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the institution remains controller of learner data and owns intervention policy · Duration: 8–12 weeks validation and pilot setup; 16–24 weeks to production
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, data scientist, integration engineer; customer student-success director, registrar, data-protection officer, safeguarding lead, counsellor champions · Support model: Business-hours support with term-time escalation cover; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Data and fairness assessment
3) Retrospective validation on historical terms
4) Case-workflow co-design with counsellors
5) Privacy, safeguarding and security sign-off
6) Advisory pilot and benefit review
deliverables: Named case owners in place for every alert route
Alert thresholds calibrated to stated support capacity
Safe empty and error states proven — no unreviewed alert reaches a learner
Fairness thresholds met in retrospective validation
Privacy and safeguarding approvals granted; audit trail proven
effort: 8–12 weeks validation and pilot setup; 16–24 weeks to production
languages: English delivery; Arabic learner-communication templates supported
